title: A feasibility claim means the outcome Business confirmed, never what a column happens to be called
request: Package T1 of the team workspace plan (Part A, item 3; the owner's W1): persist the confirmed target (event, entity, prediction time, horizon, label source, maturity rule, brief revision); have Data Science compare it with what the table's label column records and block with the missing event, why it matters, who supplies it and which task resumes; pass the same confirmed revision to ML Engineering; when Business changes the target after feasibility, mark dependent results stale and revalidate. Regression pair: on one renewal table 'failure to renew by the contractual date' passes, 'explicit cancellation only' blocks; plus paraphrases, conflicting answers, immature outcomes and a late feature. The keyword reader returns 'unsure' instead of guessing (the seat where the helper and agent arms will later let a model read).
spec: dclab-core 0.170.0: new target_contract.py (TargetContract v1, LabelDeclaration v1, TargetVerdict, agreement, read_event, EVENTS, event_label, changed); team_work TeamTask v2 (target; reads v1), TeamWork v3, REVISABLE, target_revision, confirm_target, delegate(target=), join_status counts a revised child as outstanding; meet ProblemDataCheck v2 with the blocking mismatch target_event (check(labels=, target=)); ExperienceEvent v20 (team.target.confirmed, team.target.mismatch); ledger point team.target_agreement with five state fields; conformance and main_product_experience reasons. dclab_rnd: teamspace/fixtures.py (labels, offered, terms, feasibility(ref, target), samples renewal_with_cancellations and renewal_recent), store.py (Written.changed/revised/stale/rows, confirm_target revising every task carrying the earlier answer in one transaction, delegate(target_from=)), tools.py (confirmed_outcome, save_outcome, judge_outcome; the confirm_target answer becomes the task's contract; inspect_schema, leakage_check and validate_contract judge against it; team_delegate target_from), agents.py (_needs_outcome, _check, _answered, _next_revision, blocker reports, ML Engineering reading the target as a field, the Lead passing target_from, confirm_outcome), ledger/capture.py team_target_agreement. No migration.
plan: write the core contract and the reader first, with the regression pair and the negation cases as tests
add target to TeamTask as v2 with a v1 reader, and confirm_target as the one way an answered task works again

decisions.decision: read_event returns None (an open question) for two events, none, an event said both ways, or a hedge, never the likeliest reading
decisions.why: a wrong event silently changes what 'feasible' means; an open question costs one more message, a wrong guess costs a model built on another outcome. None is also exactly the seat where the helper and agent arms may let a model read the words; whatever a model answers is still only an event code that agreement checks

decisions.decision: the label column's event is declared (LabelDeclaration), never read from its name
decisions.why: the owner's W1: 'a column called churn is insufficient'; renewed_by_date records a failure to renew, never a cancellation

decisions.decision: a changed outcome raises the brief revision and revises every task that carried the earlier answer (same response) in one store transaction; the earlier report stays as delivered until the new one supersedes it
decisions.why: revalidation needs the existing revision machinery (accept_reply refuses older revisions); editing a delivered report would rewrite what Business already read

decisions.decision: an answer that does not settle the outcome blocks with the requester as next owner, instead of asking again in the same round
decisions.why: a second question on the same brief revision would reuse the requester's claimed confirm action; the blocker is precise and agents.confirm_outcome resumes it

decisions.decision: keep the feasibility answer text unchanged for the sample's own outcome column; the confirmed outcome is in the report's evidence and limits
decisions.why: the round-trip walkthroughs and the UI pin that sentence; the report still states which outcome was checked and by which column

findings.defect: Data Science said the data could answer 'churn = explicit cancellation' on a renewal-only table
findings.scenario: renewal_v1, the person answers 'Cancellation of the subscription.': the report says 'We can score seven days before renewal' and ML Engineering states the outcome as the cancellation while training on renewed_by_date
findings.cause: feasibility checked only that the sample had renewal dates and an outcome column; the person's answer was a sentence carried in the question text
findings.fix: TargetContract on the task, LabelDeclaration per sample column, agreement() in inspect_schema and validate_contract; blocker naming the missing record, why, who supplies it (the CRM's cancellation log) and which task resumes

findings.defect: two Lead tests encoded the old behaviour: ML Engineering planned a cancellation model on a table with no cancellation record
findings.cause: the tests pinned the pre-T1 answer
findings.fix: they now use sample:renewal_with_cancellations, and assert the target carried as a field with its column cancelled_at

findings.defect: common negations were read as yes: 'we don't mean cancellation' -> explicit_cancellation
findings.scenario: renewal_with_cancellations, the person says 'We don't mean cancellations.': the task completes with cancelled_at as the outcome, the opposite of what was said
findings.cause: _BEFORE knew not/no/never and a few contractions; _AFTER needed a verb before a bare not
findings.fix: one negation vocabulary (any n't, apostrophe-less spellings, cannot, forget, irrelevant, leave out, apart from, aside); a clause with one event and any negation never affirms it; between two events only a verb's negation sets the first aside; a clause that only says no, 'too', 'also', 'as well' and a cancelled renewal leave the question open

findings.defect: after a changed outcome the Lead could join Data Science's new report with ML Engineering's report on the old outcome and call it complete
findings.scenario: deliver the Data Science and Lead lanes before ML Engineering's row after confirm_outcome
findings.cause: join_status counted a child as returned from its current report's status alone
findings.fix: a child whose current report's brief revision is below its own is outstanding

findings.defect: a brief that names the outcome ('Which accounts will cancel their subscription?') skipped the question and passed on renewed_by_date
findings.scenario: renewal_v1 with a brief that has no vague word
findings.cause: confirm_target was asked only when the brief said churn or leaving without a definition
findings.fix: _needs_outcome: ask whenever no outcome is confirmed and the brief blurs one or names one while the task reads a sample; a brief's sentence is never taken as the confirmed outcome

findings.defect: a crash between recording the answer and saving its outcome turned clear words into a false 'unsure' blocker
findings.scenario: the outcome save lost after confirm_target was claimed; the redelivered answer row only accepted the task
findings.cause: the claimed question was read as answered-without-an-outcome
findings.fix: in waiting_for_person, a claimed question with no target and clear words records the same response again (which saves the outcome; the same event again changes nothing)
refused when the initiator is not the person, when membership no longer holds (delivery.authorize), and while the task's question is open (answer it in the thread)

measurements.name: the regression pair on sample:renewal_v1
measurements.gate: lapse passes, explicit cancellation blocks with the missing record named
measurements.result: complete with renewed_by_date / blocked with 'a record of an explicit cancellation', Business, CRM cancellation log

measurements.name: reviewer's negation inputs
measurements.gate: none read as the event they negate
measurements.result: 17 of 17 now open (None); before the fix the reviewer reproduced each as one event (13 the negated one, 4 a doubtful single reading)

outcome: The task carries the outcome a person confirmed as a contract; Data Science and ML Engineering judge the table against it and block precisely when the table records another event or its outcomes are not known; a changed outcome revises every task that carried it and the Lead waits for their new answers. Not done: no route yet lets the person change the outcome from their thread (agents.confirm_outcome is the entry point for T3/T5b); a stale report is marked only by its brief revision (reads compare it), not by a stored flag; no live model run (no model is called).
lessons: A keyword reader must treat any negation in a one-event clause as 'not that event': listing negation words one by one always misses a spelling.
When a revision makes a result stale, every reader that joins results must compare revisions, not only the writer that revises.
risks: read_event is a rule: phrasing outside its vocabulary returns None and costs a question; the helper arm (B2) is where a model reads those words.
Asking whenever a brief names an outcome adds one question where the brief was already clear; it is the price of never taking a sentence as the confirmed outcome.
